summary: Depth-first rabbithole dossier for AWS Marketplace Atlas; source-anchored research pack.

facts.text: In scope: how buying MongoDB Atlas through AWS Marketplace works. That covers the listings and their pricing models, how an AWS account gets linked to an Atlas organization, how usage is metered and billed, how private offers and contracts change the terms, how this spend draws down AWS commitments (EDP/PPA), and the limits on each part.

26. When a buyer accepts a private offer, it becomes an agreement. One offer can target up to 25 AWS accounts. If the management account accepts, the offer can be shared across an AWS Organization, but member accounts that were already subscribed must accept it again. — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/buyerguide/buyer-private-offers.html 27. When a private offer agreement expires, the buyer moves to public pricing or loses the subscription, depending on product type. For SaaS contracts, renewal and upgrade offers replace the old terms with no service break. — https://docs.aws.am

AWS meters records only after the seller receives a `License Updated` event. "Records that you send before this event aren't metered." — same `[1/4]` 30. 1. MongoDB made Atlas available through AWS Marketplace in late 2017. The stated purpose was to let enterprise customers buy Atlas through AWS procurement and billing. — https://diginomica.com/mongodb-launches-atlas-aws-marketplace-hopes-woo-cloud-buyers (Derek du Preez, 2017-11-30) 2. MongoDB's own filings date that announcement to "December 2017", describing it as "making it easier for the more than 160,000 existing AWS customers to buy and consume MongoDB Atlas." — https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1441816/000144181618000019/mdb-013118xex991xearningsr.htm (8-K Ex 99.1, 2018-03-13) 3.

11. Generic AWS flow: after a buyer subscribes, AWS POSTs an opaque `x-amzn-marketplace-token` to the seller's registration URL. The registration token expires after a 4-hour window. AWS advises sellers to resolve it immediately because "it may expire after approximately one hour." This is an intra-document inconsistency in AWS's own docs. — https://docs.aws.a
